topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and presents the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Factors versus Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core nature of cancer development and debate the relative contributions of intrinsic random mutations versus environmental and lifestyle exposures.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on pathogen mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical and metabolic mechanisms through which physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how non-mutagenic factors such as chronic inflammation, tumour promotion, and host developmental stages facilitate cancer outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and determine their potency.

topics.label: Concluding Remarks on Risk, Benefit, and Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by discussing the everyday balance of risk versus benefit regarding carcinogenic exposures and summarizing key themes.
